These four encode the verify-path log-sink contract that task 2 replaced: no residual log after a failed spawn, truncation of an existing sink on reopen, and replacement of a symlinked leaf. Task 2's own tests pin the opposite contract: tests/autopilot/test_helper_recovery_v2_sinks.py::test_verification_preserves_its_outputs_on_a_spawn_failure_but_leaves_an_empty_log[absent-program|unexecutable-program] assert the log exists and is empty after a failed spawn. Measured: all six nodes pass at cce5dad and four fail here, so these are regressions, not older defects. A candidate repair that reused _open_result_sink/_close_result_sink for the log leaf made the two spawn-failure nodes green and broke the two task-2 sink nodes; it was reverted rather than shipped. No implementation satisfies both contracts without branching on a pathname, so the choice of contract and the retirement of the superseded tests belong to the completion review, which carries this as a recorded deferred item.
